newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-INDIANS CLOSER MESA PLEADS INNOCENT OF SEX CHARGES.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-INDIANS CLOSER MESA PLEADS INNOCENT OF SEX CHARGES.

text.p: Cleveland Indians closer Jose Mesa and a friend pleaded innocent Wednesday to charges of gross sexual imposition stemming from a December 22 incident here.
Mesa and his friend, 34-year-old David Blanco of Solon, Ohio, appeared for arraignment this morning before Judge Patrick Carroll at Lakewood Municipal Court.

The 30-year-old Dominican right-hander and Blanco were released on $5,000 bond after the arrest. After entering their innocent pleas, their request for a preliminary hearing was granted and set for Friday, January 17.

The preliminary hearing is conducted to determine if there is enough evidence to consider the case for review by a grand jury. The charges are fourth-degree felonies, and carry prison terms of one year or more.
According to the Lakewood Police Department's report, two 26-year-old females complained that the two men molested them in a Lakewood motel.

The report states that Mesa and Blanco met the women in the popular downtown Cleveland area called "The Flats," and Mesa took one woman's purse to entice her into his vehicle. He drove off to the motel with the woman, while Blanco and the other woman followed in a separate car.
The women told police that they went into the motel with the intention of using the restroom, retrieving the purse and leaving. Mesa and Blanco allegedly began fondling their breasts and pubic areas.

Mesa appeared in 69 games for the Indians last season, recording 39 saves and posting a 2-7 record with a 3.73 ERA. He finished second in voting for the 1995 American League Cy Young Award when he posted a club-record 46 saves.
